prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: sideswipe while changing lanes in Sugar Land, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1218; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling in the left lane of a multi-lane roadway in Sugar Land, Texas, when the vehicle attempted to move into the adjacent lane. As the lane change began, the front portion of Driver 1's vehicle struck the rear quarter panel of Driver 2's vehicle, which was positioned alongside in the same direction of travel. Both vehicles remained upright and came to rest on the shoulder without further contact. Driver 2 stated that the sideswipe happened exactly as Driver 1 described, and two independent bystanders provided statements consistent with that account. Photographs taken at the scene show scraping and displaced trim along the right side of Driver 1's vehicle and a matching area of damage on Driver 2's rear panel. A Passenger was seated in Driver 1's vehicle at the time and was observed by responding officers and bystanders. Driver 1 reported neck strain and was evaluated at the scene. Officers found no indication of prior damage to either vehicle. Driver 1 is listed as an insured operator on the policy in force at the time of the collision.
